title: Dimension formula for finite type extensions of universally catenary domains
statement: Let $R\subset S$ be an inclusion of commutative domains, with $R$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and universally catenary [def-exc-excellent-ring], and with $S$ a finite type $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. A domain is a nonzero ring without zero divisors. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be prime ideals with $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$. For a prime $\mathfrak r$ of a ring $A$, put $\kappa(\mathfrak r)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak r)$ and write $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak r)$ for the supremum of lengths of strict chains of prime ideals ending at $\mathfrak r$. Write $\operatorname{trdeg}_A B$ for transcendence degree [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then $$\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\kappa(\mathfrak q)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)+\operatorname{trdeg}_R S.$$

source.place: Tag 02IJ (lemma-dimension-formula), equality clause for a universally catenary base; lines 27520–27607.

proof.text: Present S as a quotient of P = R[X_1,...,X_n] by a surjective R-algebra map f, with prime kernel k. P is a Noetherian domain and is catenary because it is finite type over the universally catenary R. This uses only same-universe polynomial algebras, even when S has another universe.

source.place: Tag 02IJ: polynomial-fibre formula and catenary quotient-chain argument, applied to a finite polynomial presentation; field polynomial dimension uses Tags 00P1 and 00OP.

proof.text: For a field F and a prime Q of F[X_1,...,X_n], write its finite height as d and its finite residue transcendence degree as r. The minimal-component maximum formula yields a minimal prime z with dimension(F[X]/z) = d+r. Since this polynomial ring is a domain, z=0. Its dimension is n by the Noetherian polynomial dimension theorem. Consequently height(Q)+trdeg_F kappa(Q)=n. This also covers n=0.

source.place: Tag 02IJ: polynomial-fibre formula and catenary quotient-chain argument, applied to a finite polynomial presentation; field polynomial dimension uses Tags 00P1 and 00OP.

proof.text: For a prime qprime of P contracting to p, use the prime correspondence of the fibre C = kappa(p) tensor_R P to choose Q contracting to qprime. The flat fibre height formula gives height(qprime)=height(p)+height(Q). Scalar extension identifies C with kappa(p)[X_1,...,X_n], preserving heights. The canonical residue-field map kappa(qprime) -> kappa(Q) is bijective by surjectivity on stalks. It commutes with the kappa(p)-maps, checked after composition with R -> kappa(p), so the residue transcendence degrees agree. Step 2 now gives height(qprime)+trdeg_kappa(p) kappa(qprime)=height(p)+n.

source.place: Tag 02IJ: polynomial-fibre formula and catenary quotient-chain argument, applied to a finite polynomial presentation; field polynomial dimension uses Tags 00P1 and 00OP.

proof.text: For any surjection of Noetherian domains f:A -> B with A catenary, choose prime chains realizing the finite heights of ker(f), a prime q of B, and its inverse image qprime in A. A full-height chain is saturated and begins at the least prime. Inverse image carries the saturated chain in B to a saturated chain from ker(f) to qprime: an intervening prime contains the kernel and descends by the quotient prime correspondence. Concatenate with the full-height chain to ker(f). Both this chain and the full-height chain to qprime are saturated chains from zero to qprime. Catenarity equates their lengths, proving height(qprime)=height(ker(f))+height(q). This includes zero kernel and q=0.

source.place: Tag 02IJ: polynomial-fibre formula and catenary quotient-chain argument, applied to a finite polynomial presentation; field polynomial dimension uses Tags 00P1 and 00OP.

proof.text: The surjection P -> S identifies the residue fields of qprime and q as kappa(p)-algebras. Check compatibility on elements of R and extend across kappa(p) by residue-field extensionality. The same comparison at k and zero identifies kappa(k) with Frac(S) over Frac(R). The domain transcendence-degree tower formula in R -> S -> Frac(S) and R -> Frac(R) -> Frac(S) identifies the relative generic degree with trdeg_R S, since a fraction field is algebraic over its domain. Apply Cardinal.toENat to the lifted cardinal equalities to remove universe lifts.

source.place: Tag 02IJ: polynomial-fibre formula and catenary quotient-chain argument, applied to a finite polynomial presentation; field polynomial dimension uses Tags 00P1 and 00OP.

proof.text: Apply the polynomial formula of step 3 first at qprime and then at k, which contracts to zero by injectivity of R -> S. Steps 4 and 5 give height(k)+height(q)+t=height(p)+n and height(k)+trdeg_R S=n. Substitute the second equality into the first, reorder, and cancel height(k), finite by Noetherianity. The result is exactly the asserted equality with the canonical residue algebra structure.
